title: Surface Tension - lines-layer rehearsal
summary: A two-scene hand-written manifest exercising the multi-voice lines layer (#172).

lines.speaker: anchor
lines.text: You are listening to a rehearsal, which is the least promising sentence in radio, so let us get on with it.

lines.speaker: skeptic
lines.text: It is a rehearsal for a show about blog posts nobody asked to be read aloud. I want that on the record before we start.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Noted, and overruled. The whole point is that four people arguing about one post is more honest than one voice summarising it.

lines.speaker: switchboard
lines.text: Lines are open, the coffee is bad, and the board is already lit. Let us go to the first post.

lines.speaker: anchor
lines.text: First up: a post arguing that small software should stay small, and that every feature past the second one is a tax the author pays forever.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: The argument holds. The maintenance cost of a feature is not the week you wrote it, it is every week after, and most projects never price that in until they are drowning.

lines.speaker: skeptic
lines.text: It holds right up until it meets a user. The post never says who decides which two features count, and that is the entire fight, not a detail.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: The author does say it, in the part about shipping the smallest thing that is embarrassing and letting the complaints pick the third feature for you.

lines.speaker: anchor
lines.text: We will call that a draw and move on, which is the anchor's privilege and the reason this desk exists.
